_readme: The one compact format a RUN TIME is written in, for a person to read
format_elapsed (the terminal, the bootstrap's 'Took' line, the bulk
re-check) and the dashboard template's fmtElapsed. Read by
neither suite owns it, so neither side can bend a case to what it does.
Input is SECONDS (a run time's elapsed_ms / 1000). Under a second reads
'under 1s'; under a minute in whole seconds; under ten minutes as minutes
and two-digit seconds; under an hour as whole minutes; from an hour, as
hours and two-digit minutes - never days. Rounding is half up, as
JavaScript's Math.round, and is done BEFORE the unit is chosen, so 59.6s
is '1m 00s' and never '60s'. PROVISIONAL (2026-11-16): the ten-minute
point where seconds stop being shown is the builder's choice, the one
rule that gives both '1m 00s' and '45m' as the criterion asks.
